dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Do you know, in Russian, there's only one way to say "only one" but how about in Vietnamese?

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: That's interesting! In Vietnamese, we can say "chỉ", "chỉ có", or "duy nhất" to express "only one". Each word has its own nuance.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Really? So if I want to say "there's only one person who understands me", which word should I use? Sometimes I feel there's chỉ one person who truly hiểu me in this Saigon.

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: That sounds quite profound. If you want to emphasize the emotion, you should use "there's duy nhất one person who understands me". Who is that only person?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: It's... Wait, why do you want to know? It's not like you care about my thoughts, right?

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: Of course I care. Maybe I just muốn to know if that only person is me. Or perhaps I'm just one of many people who hiểu you?
